title: DECISION: Injection provenance tests use is_peerable() as oracle not routing code
description: injection_provenance_tests.rs tests the routing behavior of append_to_groups with the oracle being InjectionSource::is_peerable(), not the routing code under test. The test header comment explicitly states this: 'Oracle: expected presence/absence of group log entries is derived from InjectionSource::is_peerable(), which is the specification, NOT from reading the routing code under test.' The old-queue-file test also verifies that the serde default for missing injection_source is SmtpSieve (peerable), protecting against the failure mode where old queue files are silently dropped from the log. A future contributor might change the oracle to the routing code itself, making it a pure roundtrip test that cannot detect a bug in routing logic.
